emergence.summary: A single-gene HMBS loss-of-function partially blocks heme synthesis at the hydroxymethylbilane-synthase (porphobilinogen deaminase) step. HMBS normally consumes porphobilinogen; when it is deficient, the upstream neurotoxic precursors delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG) ACCUMULATE during attacks -> the toxic-precursor burden is driven UP. Read as a released BRAKE on precursor accumulation (HMBS brakes the build-up; LOF releases it -> burden UP), the tyrosinaemia pattern. The kit re-derives the approved therapy, which RESTRAINS the UPSTREAM rate-limiting enzyme ALAS1 rather than restoring HMBS: givosiran (an ALAS1-knockdown siRNA) and hemin (heme feedback that down-regulates ALAS1) both lower ALA/PBG production; restoring HMBS (liver transplantation; gene therapy investigational) is definitive. The gamma read is of the HMBS locus switch structure; the disease lesion is coding, outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
emergence.emergent_axis: toxic heme-precursor burden (delta-aminolevulinic acid / porphobilinogen accumulation)

grades.perturbation_direction: [F] forced by (role x mechanism); cited biology
grades.perturbation_magnitude: [O] OPEN -- how far the switch moves is runtime/Layer-2, not sequence-derivable

per_gene.note: HMBS (hydroxymethylbilane synthase / porphobilinogen deaminase) is the third enzyme of heme synthesis and consumes porphobilinogen. As a BRAKE on heme-precursor accumulation, its LOF RELEASES the brake -> the neurotoxic precursors ALA and PBG accumulate during attacks. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the coding lesion (firewall). The pathological axis is the TOXIC PRECURSOR BURDEN (it goes UP), so the corrective levers LOWER it.
per_gene.src: Grandchamp 1989 (HMBS mutations); Anderson 2005 review (ALA/PBG in AIP)

emergence.firewall: gamma reads promoter switch-threshold STRUCTURE only; perturbation DIRECTION is forced+cited; MAGNITUDE is [O] (runtime/Layer-2, not sequence-derivable).

levers.push_direction: knock down the UPSTREAM rate-limiting ALAS1 so less ALA / PBG is made -> lower the toxic-precursor burden
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] ALA/PBG-lowering magnitude / attack-rate not derived from sequence

levers.push_direction: supply heme so feedback DOWN-regulates ALAS1 -> reduce ALA / PBG production during attacks
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] feedback-repression magnitude not derived from sequence

levers.push_direction: restore HMBS so accumulating porphobilinogen is consumed again -> lower the toxic burden (definitive)
levers.agent_class: HMBS restoration (liver transplantation; HMBS gene therapy investigational)
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] degree/durability of restored HMBS activity not derived from sequence

treatment_A_switch.firewall: levers are DIRECTION + cited agent CLASS; not dose/potency/efficacy/safety, not a recommendation to treat any individual.

falsifiers.claim: HMBS LOF (released brake) raises the toxic heme-precursor burden (axis UP)
falsifiers.falsifier: an HMBS deficiency allele that LOWERED ALA / PBG accumulation would refute the released-brake direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: urinary ALA / PBG levels by HMBS genotype (during attacks)

falsifiers.claim: knocking down the upstream ALAS1 (givosiran / hemin) is the CORRECTIVE direction (lowers the burden)
falsifiers.falsifier: if ALAS1 knockdown or heme feedback RAISED or failed to lower ALA / PBG, the restrain-ALAS1 lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: urinary ALA / PBG response to ALAS1 knockdown or hemin
